planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix; Selby is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor plant.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix. Selby is a compact Homalomena selection with glossy, heart-shaped, deep green leaves on reddish, upright petioles, a tidy rosette-forming aroid related to philodendron and anthurium but with a lower, non-climbing habit that suits a tabletop or floor grouping without needing a moss pole. Its dense, clumping growth and tolerance of average indoor conditions make it a reliable, low-fuss tropical foliage plant for shaded interiors. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings, avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 55°F, and divide congested clumps in spring to propagate or refresh an overgrown pot.

common_name: Emerald Gem Homalomena (Compact Glossy-Leaf Tropical Aroid)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix; Emerald Gem is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor plant.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix. Emerald Gem forms a dense, low rosette of glossy, deep emerald-green, heart-shaped leaves, a compact, tidy Homalomena selection well suited to a small pot, terrarium border, or mixed tropical foliage grouping where a larger climbing aroid would take up too much room. It shares the same general care needs as its philodendron and anthurium relatives but grows as a non-climbing, clumping plant that stays manageable without staking. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings, avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 55°F, and divide congested clumps in spring to propagate or refresh an overgrown pot.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix; Spathicarpa is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor plant.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix. Spathicarpa sagittifolia is an unusual South American aroid with arrow-shaped leaves and a highly distinctive inflorescence: rather than a typical hooded spathe wrapped around a separate spadix, its flat, leaf-like spathe fuses directly to the spadix along its length, with tiny flowers studded across the fused surface, a botanical curiosity unlike the flower structure of any other commonly grown houseplant aroid. Its modest size and clumping habit suit a small pot or terrarium alongside other unusual foliage plants. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings, avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 55°F, and divide congested clumps in spring to propagate.

planting.note: Plant divisions or tubers after last frost when soil is warm; in zone 8-9 plant March-April. Fontanesii is root-hardy in zone 8b-11 with heavy winter mulch; farther north lift and store tubers indoors over winter.

directions: Plant in rich, moist soil in partial shade to full sun with consistent moisture; Colocasia fontanesii, commonly called violet-stem taro, produces medium-large, dark green, arrow-shaped leaves with a distinctive deep purple-violet midrib and stem that stands out sharply against the green foliage and darkens further with more sun exposure. It is more slender and upright than many of the largest elephant ear cultivars, giving it a graceful, airy look useful for adding height without the bulk of giant-leaved types. Feed regularly and keep soil consistently moist to wet through the growing season, since the plant naturally grows in marshy conditions. Where winters bring hard freezes, dig and store the tubers dry and frost-free, or in zone 8b and warmer mulch heavily and let the root-hardy tuber resprout in spring.
